teaser: A site factory: a request in a commit makes a CI pipeline create the repository, DNS record and vault, seed a page, check HTTPS and record it all.
core_idea: Every new site needs a GitHub repository, a DNS record and an sgit vault. Instead of clicks or scripts, a public CI site factory takes a request folder committed to a control repository, posts a plan on the pull request with no secrets, and on merge creates the repository, record and vault, seeds and verifies the site, optionally runs a Claude Code first pass, and writes status back, using a GitHub App and AWS OpenID Connect so no long-lived keys are stored. An agent creates a site by committing a request.

nodes.label: Plan, then apply
nodes.summary: PR plan without secrets; apply on merge.

quotes.text: The factory turns creating infrastructure into writing a file
It can create; only the teardown pipeline can remove.
What stays private is only the credentials
